sentences.text: The holotype is a partial skeleton containing the skull, lower jaws, five neck vertebrae, shoulder girdle, and most of the arms and legs.
Unfortunately, the remains are not well preserved.
The specimen represents a small individual.
Its skull is relatively large, reaching a length of 136 millimetres.
The parietal bones join at the midline to create a crest.
The snout tip curves downward in front of the lower jaw so deeply that the mouth roof aligns with the lower jaw's edge.
The front of the snout features a small premaxilla that continues the nasal line downward to form a small upper beak.
This beak is separated by a low notch from the toothless lower edge of the maxilla.
The lower jaw dentary possesses an opening on each side.
The femur is quite curved, displaying a convex anterior end.
The tibia measures 185 mm in length and is therefore very long compared to the femur; only some juvenile ornithomimid specimens have relatively larger tibiotarsi.
The foot claws are flatter than those of the hands.
The hand claws are relatively large, curved, and have a flatter underside.
The hand phalanx formula is 1-2-3-0-0 or 2-3-3-0-0, or 0-1-2-3-0/0-2-2-3-0 if the three hand digits are interpreted as the second, third, and fourth.
The upper phalanges of the second and third (or third and fourth) digits are elongated, exceeding 75% of the length of their corresponding metacarpals.
A local farmer discovered the skeleton of a small theropod at Xiaobeigou in Liaoning in the early twenty-first century.
The farmer who found the fossil attempted to restore damaged bones and added fake parts to increase its value.
The species Hexing qingyi was named and described in 2012 by Jin Liyong, Chen Jun, and Pascal Godefroit.

Although small body size was previously known only in juvenile ornithomimosaurians, this holotype is not juvenile, evidenced by the complete fusion of skull bones, cervical ribs, scapulocoracoid, and ankle bones.
Body length cannot be determined directly due to a missing spine, but the femur measures 135 mm, compared to 191 mm in the smaller ornithomimosaur Shenzhousaurus.
Hexing belongs to the parent group Ornithomimosauria and is classified as a reptile.
The type species of the genus Hexing is Hexing qingyi.
Researchers assigned Hexing a basal position within the Ornithomimosauria.
Phylogenetic analysis found Hexing to be more derived than Pelecanimimus but less advanced than Beishanlong, Garudimimus, Harpymimus, and the Ornithomimidae.
The smaller forms Hexing and Senzhousaurus are the most primitive known ornithomimosaurians, like Pelecanimimus which dates to the late Barremian.

Because this latter species is more basal, authors considered it strong evidence that a land bridge formed between Europe and Asia much earlier than the Aptian, the date usually assumed for this event.

The description of the hand situation is complicated by the fact that describers follow Xu Xing's hypothesis that in Tetanurae—including birds and Hexing—the first, second, and third digits are actually the second, third, and fourth.
Hexing qingyi lived during the early Cretaceous period between 140 and 130 million years ago in what is now Asia.
The holotype was found in the lower Yixian Formation, dating from the early Valanginian to early Barremian stage between 139 and 128 million years ago.
Hexing lived during the Barremian to Aptian, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
